title: Attention Is All You Need
venue: 31st Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NIPS 2017), Long Beach, CA, USA
tldr: The Transformer replaces recurrence with self-attention, achieving superior translation quality with far greater parallelism and lower training time.
abstract: Sequence transduction models typically rely on recurrent or convolutional layers. We propose the Transformer, a model based solely on attention mechanisms, dispensing with recurrence and convolutions. It achieves 28.4 BLEU on WMT 2014 English-to-German and 41.8 BLEU on English-to-French, surpassing prior state-of-the-art results while training faster and in parallel. The model generalizes well to other tasks, such as English constituency parsing.

blocks.text: Recurrent and convolutional neural networks dominate sequence modeling, particularly in tasks like language modeling and machine translation. These models factor computation along symbol positions, generating hidden states sequentially. This sequential nature limits parallelization within training examples, a critical bottleneck for long sequences.

Attention mechanisms allow modeling dependencies regardless of distance in input or output sequences. However, they are typically used alongside recurrent networks. We introduce the Transformer, a model that relies entirely on self-attention to draw global dependencies between input and output, enabling significantly more parallelization and faster training.

blocks.title: Key Insight
blocks.text: Self-attention replaces recurrence entirely, enabling constant-time dependency modeling and full parallelization.

Efforts to reduce sequential computation include Extended Neural GPU, ByteNet, and ConvS2S, which use convolutional layers to compute hidden representations in parallel. However, the number of operations to relate distant positions grows with distance, making it harder to learn long-range dependencies. The Transformer reduces this to a constant number of operations, though with reduced effective resolution due to averaging attention-weighted positions—a limitation mitigated by Multi-Head Attention.

Self-attention relates different positions of a single sequence to compute its representation. It has been used successfully in reading comprehension, abstractive summarization, and textual entailment. End-to-end memory networks use recurrent attention but not sequence-aligned recurrence. The Transformer is the first transduction model to rely entirely on self-attention without RNNs or convolutions.

Most competitive sequence transduction models use an encoder-decoder structure. The encoder maps an input sequence of symbol representations to a sequence of continuous representations. The decoder generates an output sequence one element at a time, auto-regressively consuming previously generated symbols.

blocks.text: Encoder and Decoder Stacks

The encoder consists of a stack of N = 6 identical layers. Each layer has two sub-layers: a multi-head self-attention mechanism and a position-wise feed-forward network. Residual connections and layer normalization are applied around each sub-layer. All sub-layers and embedding layers produce outputs of dimension d_model = 512.

The decoder also has N = 6 identical layers. In addition to the encoder’s sub-layers, the decoder includes a third sub-layer performing multi-head attention over the encoder’s output. The self-attention sub-layer is modified to prevent positions from attending to subsequent positions, ensuring auto-regressive properties.
Attention
Attention maps a query and a set of key-value pairs to an output, computed as a weighted sum of the values. The weights are derived from a compatibility function of the query with the keys.
Scaled Dot-Product Attention

Our attention mechanism, Scaled Dot-Product Attention, computes dot products of queries and keys, divides by √d_k, and applies softmax to obtain weights. For efficiency, we compute attention on packed matrices Q, K, and V. The scaling factor counteracts the effect of large dot products pushing softmax gradients into regions with extremely small values.

blocks.caption: Scaled Dot-Product Attention: queries, keys, and values are packed into matrices, and attention weights are computed via scaled dot products followed by softmax.
blocks.label: Figure 2 (left)

blocks.text: Multi-Head Attention

Instead of a single attention function, we use h = 8 parallel attention layers (heads). Each head projects queries, keys, and values into lower-dimensional spaces (d_k = d_v = 64). The outputs are concatenated and projected to the model dimension. This allows the model to jointly attend to information from different representation subspaces at different positions.

blocks.title: Multi-Head Attention
blocks.text: Multi-head attention splits the attention mechanism into multiple parallel heads, each learning to focus on different aspects of the input. This enables the model to capture diverse dependencies without averaging them into a single representation.
points: Each head operates on a lower-dimensional subspace (d_k = d_v = 64).
Outputs are concatenated and linearly projected to the model dimension (d_model = 512).
Total computational cost is similar to single-head attention with full dimensionality.

blocks.caption: Multi-Head Attention: multiple attention heads run in parallel, each with its own learned projections for queries, keys, and values.
blocks.label: Figure 2 (right)

blocks.text: Applications of Attention

The Transformer uses multi-head attention in three ways: encoder-decoder attention (queries from decoder, keys/values from encoder), encoder self-attention (all from encoder output), and decoder self-attention (masked to prevent leftward information flow).
Position-wise Feed-Forward Networks

Each encoder and decoder layer includes a feed-forward network applied to each position separately. This consists of two linear transformations with a ReLU activation in between. The inner layer has dimensionality d_ff = 2048, while input and output dimensions are d_model = 512.
Embeddings and Softmax

Learned embeddings convert input and output tokens to vectors of dimension d_model. A learned linear transformation and softmax convert decoder outputs to predicted next-token probabilities. We share weights between embedding layers and the pre-softmax linear transformation, scaling the embedding weights by √d_model.
Positional Encoding

Since the Transformer lacks recurrence or convolution, we inject positional information using positional encodings. These are added to input embeddings and use sine and cosine functions of different frequencies:

blocks.title: Positional Encoding
blocks.text: Positional encodings allow the model to use the order of the sequence. We use sinusoidal functions with geometrically increasing wavelengths, enabling the model to learn relative positions via linear combinations.
points: Each dimension corresponds to a sinusoid with a unique wavelength.

blocks.text: Learned positional embeddings performed nearly identically to sinusoidal encodings, but we chose the latter for its potential to extrapolate to longer sequences.

We compare self-attention to recurrent and convolutional layers for mapping variable-length sequences. Three key metrics are considered: total computational complexity per layer, parallelization potential, and path length between long-range dependencies.

Self-attention connects all positions with a constant number of sequential operations, while recurrent layers require O(n) operations. For sequence lengths n smaller than the representation dimension d, self-attention is faster. Convolutional layers require O(n/k) or O(log_k(n)) layers to connect distant positions, increasing path length.

blocks.title: Advantages of Self-Attention
blocks.text: Self-attention offers constant-time dependency modeling, full parallelization, and shorter paths for long-range dependencies compared to recurrent or convolutional layers.
Self-attention may also yield more interpretable models. Attention distributions often reflect syntactic and semantic structure, with individual heads learning distinct tasks.
Training Data and Batching

We trained on WMT 2014 English-German (4.5M sentence pairs) and English-French (36M sentences). Sentences were encoded using byte-pair encoding (shared vocabulary of 37K tokens for EN-DE) and word-piece encoding (32K tokens for EN-FR). Batches contained ~25K source and target tokens each.
Hardware and Schedule

Models were trained on one machine with 8 NVIDIA P100 GPUs. Base models took ~0.4 seconds per step and trained for 100K steps (12 hours). Big models took ~1.0 second per step and trained for 300K steps (3.5 days).
Optimizer
We used the Adam optimizer with β₁ = 0.9, β₂ = 0.98, and ε = 10⁻⁹. The learning rate varied as lrate = d_model^(-0.5) · min(step_num^(-0.5), step_num · warmup_steps^(-1.5)), with warmup_steps = 4000.
Regularization

We applied residual dropout (P_drop = 0.1 for base models, 0.3 for big models) to sub-layer outputs and embedding sums. Label smoothing (ε_ls = 0.1) improved accuracy and BLEU scores despite hurting perplexity.
Machine Translation

On WMT 2014 English-to-German, the big Transformer model achieved 28.4 BLEU, surpassing prior state-of-the-art by over 2.0 BLEU. On English-to-French, it achieved 41.8 BLEU, a new single-model state-of-the-art, at a fraction of the training cost of prior models.
For inference, we used beam search with a beam size of 4 and length penalty α = 0.6. Checkpoint averaging (last 5 for base, last 20 for big) improved results.
Model Variations

We evaluated the impact of varying components of the Transformer on EN-DE development set (newstest2013). Key findings: multi-head attention outperforms single-head; larger models and dropout improve performance; sinusoidal and learned positional encodings perform similarly.
English Constituency Parsing

A 4-layer Transformer with d_model = 1024 achieved 91.3 F1 on WSJ Section 23 (WSJ-only training) and 92.7 F1 in a semi-supervised setting, outperforming most prior models despite minimal task-specific tuning.
Attention heads often exhibit interpretable behavior, such as tracking long-distance dependencies, resolving anaphora, or reflecting syntactic structure.

blocks.text: The Transformer is the first sequence transduction model based entirely on self-attention, replacing recurrent layers with multi-headed self-attention. It achieves superior translation quality with greater parallelism and lower training time, setting new state-of-the-art results on WMT 2014 EN-DE and EN-FR. The model generalizes well to other tasks, such as English constituency parsing, and offers interpretable attention patterns.
Future work includes extending the Transformer to other modalities (e.g., images, audio, video) and investigating local, restricted attention mechanisms for large inputs.
«The Transformer is the first transduction model relying entirely on self-attention to compute representations of its input and output without using sequence-aligned RNNs or convolution.»

blocks.text: The Transformer follows the encoder-decoder structure. The encoder maps an input sequence of symbol representations to a sequence of continuous representations z. Given z, the decoder generates an output sequence one element at a time.

blocks.caption: The Transformer model architecture: stacked self-attention and feed-forward layers for encoder and decoder.
blocks.label: Figure 1

blocks.text: Encoder and Decoder Stacks

Each encoder layer has two sub-layers: a multi-head self-attention mechanism and a position-wise fully connected feed-forward network. Each decoder layer adds a third sub-layer: multi-head attention over the encoder output. We employ a residual connection around each sub-layer, followed by layer normalization: LayerNorm(x + Sublayer(x)).
The decoder’s self-attention is masked to prevent attending to future positions, preserving auto-regression.
Attention: The Engine

blocks.title: Scaled Dot-Product Attention
blocks.text: Computes attention as a weighted sum of values, where weights are softmax of scaled dot products between queries and keys.
points: Scaling by 1/√dₖ prevents softmax gradients from vanishing for large dₖ.
Dot-product attention is faster and more space-efficient than additive attention.

blocks.caption: Scaled Dot-Product Attention: queries, keys, and values are packed into matrices Q, K, V.
blocks.label: Figure 2 (left)

blocks.title: Multi-Head Attention
blocks.text: Projects queries, keys, and values h times into lower-dimensional subspaces, computes attention in parallel, and concatenates results.
points: Allows the model to jointly attend to information from different representation subspaces.
With h = 8, dₖ = dᵥ = d_model / h = 64, computational cost is similar to single-head attention.

blocks.caption: Multi-Head Attention: parallel attention layers with learned projections.
blocks.label: Figure 2 (right)

blocks.text: The Transformer uses multi-head attention in three ways: encoder-decoder attention (queries from decoder, keys/values from encoder), encoder self-attention, and decoder self-attention (masked).
Positional Encoding

Since our model contains no recurrence and no convolution, we add positional encodings to input embeddings to inject order information. We use sine and cosine functions of different frequencies: PE(pos, 2i) = sin(pos / 10000^(2i/d_model)), PE(pos, 2i+1) = cos(pos / 10000^(2i/d_model)).
This allows the model to extrapolate to longer sequences than seen during training.
Feed-Forward and Embeddings

Each layer contains a position-wise feed-forward network: FFN(x) = max(0, xW₁ + b₁)W₂ + b₂, with d_model = 512 and d_ff = 2048. We use learned embeddings to convert input/output tokens to vectors of dimension d_model, and share weights between embedding layers and the pre-softmax linear transformation, scaled by √d_model.
Self-attention connects all positions with a constant number of sequentially executed operations, whereas a recurrent layer requires O(n) sequential operations.

For sequence length n smaller than representation dimensionality d, self-attention is faster than recurrent layers. Convolutional layers are generally more expensive than recurrent layers by a factor of k (kernel size), and even with separable convolutions, the complexity equals self-attention plus feed-forward.

blocks.title: Key advantage
blocks.text: Self-attention provides constant path length for long-range dependencies, making it easier to learn them.
We trained on WMT 2014 EN-DE (4.5M sentence pairs, byte-pair encoding, 37K tokens) and EN-FR (36M sentences, word-piece, 32K tokens). Each batch contained ~25K source and target tokens.
We used Adam optimizer with β₁ = 0.9, β₂ = 0.98, ε = 10⁻⁹, and a learning rate schedule: lrate = d_model⁻⁰·⁵ · min(step_num⁻⁰·⁵, step_num · warmup_steps⁻¹·⁵), with warmup_steps = 4000.
Regularization: residual dropout (P_drop = 0.1 for base, 0.3 for big), label smoothing (ε_ls = 0.1).
Base models trained for 100K steps (12 hours on 8 P100 GPUs), big models for 300K steps (3.5 days).

«Our model achieves 28.4 BLEU on the WMT 2014 English-to-German translation task, improving over the existing best results, including ensembles, by over 2 BLEU. On the WMT 2014 English-to-French translation task, our model establishes a new single-model state-of-the-art BLEU score of 41.8 after training for 3.5 days on eight GPUs, a small fraction of the training costs of the best models from the literature.»
«The Transformer generalizes well to other tasks by applying it successfully to English constituency parsing both with large and limited training data.»
We found that multi-head attention with h = 8, dₖ = dᵥ = 64 works best, and that bigger models (d_model = 1024, d_ff = 4096) improve performance.
Many of the attention heads clearly learn to perform different tasks, many appear to exhibit behavior related to the syntactic and semantic structure of the sentences.

blocks.text: Recurrent and convolutional models dominate sequence transduction but suffer from sequential computation (RNNs) or limited long-range dependency modeling (convolutions). Training is slow, and parallelization is constrained.

RNNs (LSTMs, GRUs) and CNNs (ByteNet, ConvS2S) were state-of-the-art. Attention mechanisms (Bahdanau et al., 2014) augmented these but did not replace recurrence. Self-attention (Parikh et al., 2016) was used in isolation but not as the sole building block for transduction.

blocks.title: Key gap
blocks.text: No prior model relied entirely on self-attention for both encoder and decoder.

The Transformer is an encoder-decoder architecture with stacked layers of multi-head self-attention and position-wise feed-forward networks. It replaces recurrence with self-attention, enabling constant-time path length between any two positions.

blocks.title: Scaled Dot-Product Attention
blocks.text: Computes attention weights as softmax(QKᵀ / √dₖ)V, where Q, K, V are queries, keys, values. Scaling by √dₖ prevents gradient vanishing for large dₖ.
points: Q, K, V are matrices of dimensions (n, dₖ) or (n, dᵥ).
Output is a weighted sum of values, with weights derived from query-key compatibility.

blocks.title: Multi-Head Attention
blocks.text: Splits Q, K, V into h heads (h=8), each with reduced dimension dₖ = d_model/h. Runs attention in parallel per head, concatenates outputs, and projects back to d_model.
points: Allows the model to attend to information from different representation subspaces.
Total computation cost is similar to single-head attention with full dimensionality.

blocks.title: Positional Encoding
blocks.text: Adds sinusoidal positional encodings to input embeddings to inject sequence order. Uses sine/cosine functions with geometrically increasing wavelengths (2π to 10000·2π).

blocks.title: Architecture
blocks.text: Encoder: N=6 identical layers, each with multi-head self-attention + position-wise FFN (d_ff=2048), residual connections, and layer normalization. Decoder: same as encoder but with an additional multi-head attention layer over encoder outputs and masking to prevent attending to future positions.
points: d_model=512 for base model, 1024 for big model.
Shared embedding weights between encoder/decoder and pre-softmax layer.

blocks.text: Outperforms all prior models (including ensembles) on EN-DE by >2 BLEU and sets new single-model SOTA on EN-FR, with 1/4 the training cost. Generalizes to parsing, matching or exceeding prior SOTA.

items: Downsides: O(n²·d) memory for self-attention limits sequence length; quadratic complexity for long sequences.
Open questions: Can restricted self-attention (e.g., local windows) maintain performance for very long sequences?
Worth pursuing: Yes. Self-attention enables parallelization, long-range dependencies, and interpretable attention patterns. The Transformer is now the foundation for most modern NLP models.

blocks.text: The Transformer replaces recurrence with self-attention, achieving state-of-the-art results in translation and parsing with faster training and better parallelization. Its simplicity, efficiency, and effectiveness make it a landmark architecture for sequence modeling.

readerIssue.title: Self-attention and positional encoding
readerIssue.text: Readers may struggle with how the Transformer replaces recurrence with self-attention while preserving sequence order. The paper introduces positional encodings (sine/cosine functions) to inject positional information into the model, allowing it to attend to tokens based on their relative or absolute positions without sequential processing.

importance.verdict: This paper introduced the Transformer architecture, revolutionizing NLP by replacing RNNs/CNNs with self-attention, enabling parallelization and state-of-the-art results.

mustRead.title: Scaled Dot-Product Attention definition
mustRead.why: Core innovation: the attention mechanism that replaces recurrence, enabling parallel computation.
mustRead.excerpt: We call our particular attention 'Scaled Dot-Product Attention' (Figure 2). The input consists of queries and keys of dimension d_k, and values of dimension d_v. We compute the dot products of the query with all keys, divide each by sqrt(d_k), and apply a softmax function to obtain the weights on the values. In practice, we compute the attention function on a set of queries simultaneously, packed together into a matrix Q. The keys and values are also packed together into matrices K and V. We compute the matrix of outputs as: Attention(Q, K, V) = softmax(QK^T / sqrt(d_k))V.

mustRead.title: Multi-Head Attention rationale
mustRead.why: Explains how multi-head attention allows the model to attend to different representation subspaces, a key improvement over single-head attention.
mustRead.excerpt: Instead of performing a single attention function with d_model-dimensional keys, values and queries, we found it beneficial to linearly project the queries, keys and values h times with different, learned linear projections to d_k, d_k and d_v dimensions, respectively. On each of these projected versions of queries, keys and values we then perform the attention function in parallel, yielding d_v-dimensional output values. These are concatenated and once again projected, resulting in the final values.

mustRead.title: Positional Encoding design
mustRead.why: Critical for understanding how the Transformer handles sequence order without recurrence or convolution.
mustRead.excerpt: Since our model contains no recurrence and no convolution, in order for the model to make use of the order of the sequence, we must inject some information about the relative or absolute position of the tokens in the sequence. To this end, we add 'positional encodings' to the input embeddings at the bottoms of the encoder and decoder stacks. We use sine and cosine functions of different frequencies: PE_(pos, 2i) = sin(pos / 10000^(2i/d_model)), PE_(pos, 2i+1) = cos(pos / 10000^(2i/d_model)).

mustRead.title: Why Self-Attention (Table 1)
mustRead.why: Quantifies the advantages of self-attention over RNNs/CNNs in terms of parallelization and path length for long-range dependencies.
mustRead.excerpt: A self-attention layer connects all positions with a constant number of sequentially executed operations, whereas a recurrent layer requires O(n) sequential operations. In terms of computational complexity, self-attention layers are faster than recurrent layers when the sequence length n is smaller than the representation dimensionality d. The maximum path length between any two input and output positions in networks composed of self-attention layers is O(1), compared to O(n) for recurrent layers and O(log_k(n)) for convolutional layers.
